subject: Energy
title: Tesla and Alternating Current
description: Learn Tesla and Alternating Current in one minute.

hook.text: Nikola Tesla championed alternating current—electricity that reverses direction many times per second.

buildup.text: AC could be stepped up to high voltages for long-distance transmission—then stepped down for safe use in homes.

discovery.text: Tesla's polyphase AC motor (1888) was elegant and efficient—it could power industrial machines without sparking brushes.

twist.text: George Westinghouse funded Tesla's vision—together they lit the 1893 Chicago World's Fair with dazzling AC power.

climax.text: The Niagara Falls power plant (1895) transmitted AC electricity 26 miles to Buffalo—proving long-distance power worked.

punchline.text: Tesla's AC won—electricity could now travel hundreds of miles.

quiz.question: Why is AC better than DC for long-distance transmission?
options: Voltage can be stepped up to reduce losses
